Contrato por proyecto de 3 meses.
Modalidad 100% remoto
Horario de oficina.

The Administrative Assistant to the Marshal/Events Services Coordinator is a principal support services specialist for the Marshal's Office in the Supreme Court of the United States.

The incumbent has principal responsibility for event management, provides administrative support for oral argument sessions and a variety of other support activities and programs.

Works directly with high-level officials, outside vendors and contractors; responsible for researching, designing, planning, coordinating, and evaluating all events and programs under the direction of the Staff Assistant/Event Services Manager.

Must be present for all assigned events (approximately 900 yearly) that occur in the Supreme Court, including after-hour events (approximately 50 yearly).

Constantly faced with changing workloads, short deadlines and unanticipated requirements; logistical planning factors include room setup, rental equipment, audiovisual support, security, media, florists, transportation, entertainment, décor, and effectively integrating internal support staff and outside vendors.

Assists with menu selections, initiates requests for proposals and negotiates catering contracts; assigns the duties of the Supreme Court Police, Building Support Services, Architect of the Capitol staff, and Purveyor staff in connection with each event and maintains financial records.

Acts as the official Courtroom Timekeeper during oral argument; operates Teleconference Bridge for remote participants; works with IT to troubleshoot equipment.

Responsible for receiving visitors, responding to and following through on telephone calls and emails, preparing and distributing correspondence and responsible for completing various assigned projects in a timely manner. Performs other duties as assigned by the Marshal.
Five years of experience with event management and support services procedures are required.

A working knowledge of the Marshal's Office and the various offices of the Supreme Court, the Federal Judiciary and the Federal Government is desired; skill in gathering data and applying sound analyses; superior communications skills, both oral and written; sound judgment, tact, a very courteous demeanor and the ability to interact effectively with high-ranking officials and the general public are required; initiative and the ability to work independently within a team environment are also required.

For this role, you will support a busy U.S.-based neurology practice that values accurate documentation, thoughtful patient communication, and people who look for better ways to get work done.

About the Role As a Bilingual Medical Virtual Assistant, you will help keep patient and administrative workflows organized from intake through documentation and follow-up.

You will communicate with English- and Spanish-speaking patients, including patients referred by law firms, while coordinating appointments, referrals, medical records, and attorney requests.

You will also review and clean AI-generated medical notes, making this a strong opportunity for someone who combines healthcare experience with curiosity about emerging technology. This role offers meaningful autonomy and is best suited to someone who thinks critically, solves problems proactively, and can adapt as workflows evolve.

Responsibilities Manage patient intake and ensure demographic, insurance, referral, and case information is complete and accurate Schedule, confirm, and coordinate patient appointments while maintaining clear communication with patients and the clinical team Communicate professionally in English and Spanish with patients, law firm representatives, attorneys, and healthcare partners Support patients referred by law firms by tracking documentation, appointments, and required follow-up Review and clean AI-generated medical notes for clarity, formatting, completeness, and obvious inconsistencies before final review Prepare and coordinate medical referrals, ensuring supporting records and documentation are included Send requested medical documentation and case updates to attorneys through approved communication channels Maintain accurate, organized, and current patient records within the Electronic Health Records system Use Gmail, Google Drive, Google Chat, Google Meet, and other Google Workspace tools to manage communication and documentation Identify workflow gaps and recommend practical improvements that reduce errors, delays, or repetitive administrative work Requirements Must-Have: Full professional fluency in English and Spanish, both written and spoken Experience supporting a U.S. medical practice or healthcare provider Hands-on experience with patient scheduling, intake, referrals, and medical documentation Confidence using Electronic Health Records systems Strong computer skills and experience with Google Workspace, including Gmail, Drive, Chat, and Meet Excellent organization, written communication, and attention to detail Availability to work Monday through Friday during Pacific Standard Time business hours Nice to Have: Experience supporting a neurology, personal injury, legal-medical, or specialist healthcare practice Experience communicating with attorneys, law firms, or patients involved in legal cases Familiarity with AI tools such as ChatGPT or Claude Experience reviewing AI-generated notes, transcripts, or clinical documentation A track record of improving administrative processes or creating more efficient workflows Benefits Access to a $200K+ perk marketplace with discounts on 150+ global services.

The company is a dynamic real estate firm that specializes in value-add commercial properties. This includes buying, renovating, bringing in tenants, and then refinancing or reselling the properties.

The ideal candidate will be highly organized, self-managing, and comfortable handling critical real estate documentation and communication. Responsibilities

Position Overview: At Ready Roles, we don’t just fill positions; we build lasting, impactful careers. As a Remote Executive Assistant, you will step into a critical role as a trusted “right arm” for an American business owner, making an essential difference in their day-to-day and long-term success.

We are looking for driven, proactive individuals who don’t wait for instructions but actively seek opportunities to make an impact. This role is for self-starters who thrive on finding solutions, tackling new challenges, and staying one step ahead of the business owner’s needs.

Ready Roles carefully vets every client to ensure a respectful, growth-oriented work environment where your contributions are valued. We’re looking for someone ready to build a future, grow their skills, and commit to long-term success with their client. Why Join Ready Roles?

A Career Path, Not Just a Job: This isn’t a stepping-stone; it’s a role designed for long-term growth. We’re looking for candidates who are eager to build a stable career with a supportive company that invests in their future.

Independence and Opportunity to Lead: Our clients want self-driven assistants who identify opportunities for improvement, find ways to make the business run smoothly, and drive the organization forward without needing to be told what to do. You’ll actively manage the business owner’s schedule and push organizational goals, not just your own tasks.

Respectful, Growth-Focused Clients: We only partner with clients who value stability and respect for their team. As a Ready Role, you’ll work with a business owner who is committed to your success and who shares a long-term vision for growth. Key Responsibilities: 1.

Daily Management and Proactive Support: Calendar and Schedule Management: Oversee and prioritize the CEO’s calendar, blocking time for high-priority tasks, scheduling meetings, and ensuring the CEO is fully prepared for each day.

Email and Communication Oversight: Sort, prioritize, and respond to emails and messages, filtering essential information to keep the CEO focused and eliminating routine communication distractions.

Daily Check-Ins and Task Planning: Conduct a daily check-in with the CEO to review priorities, set action items, and address any immediate needs, keeping both the CEO and the team on track. 2.

Self-Directed Task Identification: Identify Areas to Add Value: Proactively seek out tasks or projects that align with business goals, whether improving internal processes, coordinating with team members, or streamlining workflows.

Manage and Anticipate Owner’s Needs: Track ongoing projects, follow up on open items, and keep the CEO informed on key updates and deadlines without needing reminders ￼. 3. Invoicing & Accounts Support
Send out invoices promptly and accurately
Monitor invoice status and ensure payments are received
Follow up on unpaid invoices (e.g., after 1 week)
Maintain detailed and organized invoicing records with clear notes (e.g., date sent, follow-ups required)
Assist with tracking company expenses and maintaining financial spreadsheets
What We’re Looking For: Self-Driven, Proactive Mindset - This role is for someone who naturally takes the initiative and actively finds ways to contribute. You’ll be expected to add value without waiting for instructions and to be a driving force for the business. Commitment to Long-Term Growth - Ready Roles is built on loyalty and stability.

We’re looking for someone who values a long-term commitment, seeks stability, and is motivated to build a future with us and the business owner they support. Aligned with Our Values - Ready Roles believes in accountability, respect, and integrity.

We’re looking for someone who takes ownership of their work, consistently shows up with purpose, and is eager to create a lasting impact.

Qualifications: Must be based in the Philippines Must have basic accounting (invoicing) knowledge and experience Must know how to utilize QuickBooks 18 years old and above Willing to work from home with a stable internet connection Must have own equipment — reliable laptop or PC and a noise-cancelling headset Available to work full-time (40 hours per week) Leadership Potential and Vision: Prior experience managing remote tasks or supporting a business owner is a plus, but we’re most interested in candidates ready to take ownership, lead by example, and actively shape the future of their role.

Resourceful and Solution-Oriented: You’ll look for ways to make the business owner’s day-to-day run smoothly, identifying gaps, solving problems, and proactively contributing to long-term growth.

Strong Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills to maintain consistent, professional interactions with the business owner, team members, and clients. Growth-Minded and Self-Motivated: If you’re looking for a career where you can make an impact and build something lasting, Ready Roles is the place for you.

This role is designed for someone who sees this as more than just a job—a chance to lead, grow, and secure their future. Apply Today If you’re ready to commit, lead, and build a career with purpose, stability, and growth, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today to join Ready Roles and start building a future where your work drives real impact, stability, and lasting success. Originally posted on Himalayas

This position is in the Supreme Court of the United States, Police Force Administrative Services Unit. The Executive Assistant for the Police Force reports to and receives general direction and supervision from the Administrative Services Unit, Administrative Officer.

However, the individual will directly support the Chief of Police, Deputy Chief of Police, and other Police Leadership staff as designated by the Chief of Police or their designee. The incumbent regularly works with Police leadership to draft written materials and perform a variety of special and complex assignments on behalf of the Chief of Police.

The Executive Assistant's core responsibilities include assisting the Police Executive Team (e.g., Chief of Police, Deputy Chief of Police, and Captains) with compiling reports, responding to inquiries, reconciling and tracking information, and drafting and managing correspondence.

Other major duties include: project management, budget tracking and contracting responsibilities; managing office administration including calendars, schedules, meetings, and travel; research on specialized topics; assisting with other program areas within the department; and providing back-up support with clearance requests, badging and fingerprinting.

At times, the incumbent may be responsible for driving executives, documents, supplies, or equipment to and from events. The incumbent may perform other duties as assigned.
A minimum of four years of office experience is required. Experience working successfully under pressure in a busy office is preferred. Outstanding attention to detail, strong organizational skills, tact, and a courteous demeanor are required. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Word is required.

Experience working in a police force, security, or judicial environment is preferable, but not required. Valid driver's license is required. Knowledge and Skills: Strong organizational, communication, and administrative skills, along with proficiency in office software, and the ability to handle complex information.

Key knowledge areas include departmental policies and procedures, federal contract management, booking travel, and records management. Crucial skills involve multitasking, independent judgment, maintaining confidentiality and positive interpersonal interactions with diverse individuals.

Considerable skill in: Following complex and varied oral and written instructions. Establishing and maintaining effective work relationships with associates and the public. Operation of office and computer equipment, including working knowledge of databases, spreadsheets, and word processing software.

Understanding and interpreting policies, directions, and procedures applicable to the Supreme Court, Marshal's Office, and Police Force. Must be able and willing to drive a motor vehicle with passengers to work events.

This position serves as an Administrative Assistant providing administrative support to the Office of the Executive Director for Operations and the Office of Small Business and Civil Rights, or equivalent organization.

At the GG-09 level, the Administrative Assistant: Supports leadership by maintaining calendars, scheduling meetings, coordinating logistics, and aligning activities with office priorities. Reviews and formats correspondence, reports, and briefing materials prepared for leadership.

Assists in tracking controlled correspondence and action items, ensuring materials flow properly through routing and concurrence pathways. Responds to incoming calls, inquiries, and visitors to the front office, directing matters appropriately and identifying items requiring leadership awareness.

Supports cross-office coordination by maintaining reference files, records, and shared resources needed for senior-level meetings. Prepares domestic travel logistics, coordinating with program offices and administrative contacts. Applies NRC security protocols when handling sensitive or protected information with supervisory guidance.

Identifies basic process improvements to enhance workflow efficiency. At the GG-10 level, the Administrative Assistant: Provides full administrative support to leadership-independently managing dynamic schedules, coordinating high-visibility meetings, ensuring alignment with agency priorities, and adjusting rapidly to shifting demands.

Prepares, edits, and finalizes correspondence, reports, presentations, and controlled action items, ensuring accuracy and compliance with NRC Management Directive 3.57 and the NRC Editorial Style Guide.

Conducts quality reviews of controlled correspondence and action items prepared for leadership signature, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and proper coordination across NRC offices. Coordinates administrative activities, convening Administrative Assistants from program offices to achieve consistent standards, processes, and communication flow.

Provides training, onboarding, and guidance to administrative staff supporting related activities, promoting uniform front-office administrative practices.

Serves as liaison between leadership and senior-level stakeholders-including Commissioners' offices, headquarters offices, regional leadership, and external partners-ensuring information flow and awareness of key commitments.

Uses Office365, Teams, SharePoint, and workflow systems to manage routing, approvals, document preparation, coordination, and leadership communication. Coordinates complex domestic and international travel, including itinerary development, logistical coordination with hosting organizations, and preparation of complete travel packages.

Handles controlled information-such as Safeguards, SUNSI, and other sensitive categories-in full compliance with NRC security policies and internal protocols. Recommends and helps implement administrative process improvements that enhance efficiency, responsiveness, and coordination with program offices.

At the GG-11 level, the Administrative Assistant: Provides advanced, executive-level administrative support to the senior leadership team, ensuring seamless coordination of high-priority commitments, agencywide initiatives, and external engagements.

Independently manages complex schedules and strategic engagements, anticipating needs and mitigating conflicts.

Develops, organizes, and finalizes high-level briefing packages, decision papers, pre-meeting materials, and sensitive correspondence used by leadership in interactions with the Commission, Congressional staff, Federal agencies, international delegations, and industry executives.

Reviews sensitive and pre-decisional materials for policy alignment and accuracy, coordinating with senior staff for final approval.

Oversees program wide administrative processes, ensuring consistency in workflow, information management, and coordination for governance bodies such as the Executive Council, Program Review Committee, and agency strategic initiatives.

Serves as the primary administrative focal point between leadership and executive-level internal/external stakeholders, ensuring leadership has timely situational awareness and that inquiries, issues, and commitments are addressed promptly.

Leads all aspects of domestic and international travel planning for senior leaders, including securing clearances, coordinating with foreign governments or international organizations, preparing briefing books, and managing all associated logistics.

Applies expert judgment when handling classified, Safeguards, SUNSI, and other controlled information, ensuring strict adherence to NRC security and information-handling requirements. Identifies operational gaps across administrative workflows and proposes solutions that improve effectiveness, communication, and leadership readiness.

Performs other duties as assigned.
In order to qualify for this position, you must have at least one year of specialized experience at the next lower grade level in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE is defined as: GG-9 Experience providing foundational administrative support, including managing calendars and meetings, formatting correspondence, routing controlled actions, maintaining office records, supporting front-office inquiries, preparing travel, applying security protocols with guidance, and suggesting basic workflow improvements.

GG-10 Experience independently managing complex schedules and high-visibility meetings; preparing, editing, and finalizing correspondence and controlled documents; reviewing materials for coordination and accuracy; standardizing administrative practices across offices; training staff; liaising with senior stakeholders; coordinating domestic and international travel; handling sensitive information under policy; and improving administrative processes.

GG-11 Experience providing executive-level support, independently managing strategic schedules and engagements; producing high-level briefings and decision materials; reviewing sensitive/pre-decisional content for alignment; overseeing agency-wide administrative workflows; serving as primary point of contact for executive stakeholders; leading domestic/international travel planning with clearances and briefing materials; handling classified/controlled information with expert judgment; and identifying systemic improvements across administrative operations To qualify for this position, you must have at least one year of specialized experience at the next lower grade level (GG-08 for consideration at the GG-09 level, GG-09 for consideration at the GG-10 level, and GG-10 for consideration at the GG-11 level), or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

The ideal candidate will be able to demonstrate the following: 1. Demonstrated skill with computer-based applications, including Office365, ADAMS, E-Concurrence, Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, and other database applications (i.e. maintaining automated tracking systems.) 2.

Demonstrated ability to provide administrative support in a variety of areas (time and attendance reporting, travel, etc.). 3. Writes in a clear, concise, and organized manner.

Knowledge of proper grammar, spelling, and punctuation, and correspondence procedures sufficient to prepare and review outgoing material for correctness, proper format, and completeness. 4. Demonstrated ability to work efficiently in handling multiple assignments with competing priorities, often under considerable pressure to meet deadlines. 5.

Demonstrated ability to deal tactfully, efficiently and professionally with all levels of personnel, and to work collaboratively within a team. A description of how you possess the specialized experience as well as how you meet the qualifications desired in an ideal candidate must be addressed in your resume.

The NRC encourages applicants to provide job experience details in your resume. Applicants may also use the supplemental vacancy question to provide additional information pertaining to the specialized experience and ideal candidate criteria. PLEASE BE CLEAR AND CONCISE. WE WILL NOT MAKE ASSUMPTIONS REGARDING YOUR EXPERIENCE.

At VÆRIDION, we are pioneering the future of sustainable regional aviation. As we continue to grow, we are looking for an exceptionally organized, proactive, and reliable Executive Assistant (all genders) to support our CEO in all day-to-day matters, from scheduling and coordination to hands-on logistical support. You will be the organizational backbone of the CEO office. You will manage complex calendars, coordinate high-level meetings, and ensure the CEO’s time is used efficiently.

Independently manage and coordinate the CEO’s calendar, appointments, meetings, and business trips.
Serve as the primary contact for internal and external stakeholders, ensuring clear and professional communication in both German and English.
Prepare meeting materials, take minutes, and ensure timely follow-up on action items.
Handle confidential information and documents with absolute discretion and maintaining structured records.
Organize travel itineraries, company events, and logistics, including occasional driving or transport support for the CEO.
Proactively anticipate needs, solve challenges before they arise, and enable the CEO to focus on strategic priorities.
Oversee smooth daily operations within the CEO Office with exceptional attention to detail and structure.

Proven experience as an Executive Assistant or in a comparable high-responsibility support role.
Outstanding organizational and time-management skills and clear attention to detail.
Excellent communication skills in English and German.
Tech-savvy, with experience using modern productivity tools (MS Office, Slack, etc.).
Professional presence, discretion, and reliability.
Valid driver’s license and willingness to drive or accompany the CEO as needed.
Hands-on mindset, flexibility, and enthusiasm for working in a dynamic startup environment.
We recognize that women and other under-represented groups are often overlooked in our industry. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every listed qualification, we still encourage you to apply. Talent and potential can’t always be captured in a checklist.

We’re looking for someone highly organized, calm, self-motivated, and adaptable.

Internal organisation and steering. You run the CEO's operating rhythm. Calendar, inbox triage, meeting preparation, and follow-through all sit with you. You keep an eye on details and you keep the leadership cadence (weeklies, board preparation, offsites) moving.
External travel and speaking. You plan and book complex international travel end to end, and you manage the speaking pipeline: inbound requests, selection, briefing packs, and logistics on the ground.
C-level relationship management. You become the trusted point of contact for the CEO's most important external relationships: customers, partners, and investors. You track who needs a touchpoint and when, and protect these relationships through reliability and proactivity.
Augmentation and anticipation. You work half a step ahead of everyone else in the room. You can identify a bottleneck before it forms. You build the systems, defaults and briefings that let the CEO spend their time on judgement rather than logistics.
Admin. You manage expenses and finance admin and can support with occasional personal assistant (PA) duties as needed.
CEO office collaboration. You’ll work in very close coordination with the CEO office, which includes a Chief of Staff and CEO Office Manager who are responsible for operational processes in the CEO office. Incl. performance management, KPI tracking, leadership accountability and strategic projects.
You Might Be a Fit If…
You have previously supported a CEO or equivalent in a demanding organisation and are looking for another environment that gives you an opportunity to grow.
You want to be in a young, fast company. You are comfortable with ambiguity, short timelines and a team that is still writing its own playbook, and you would rather shape the system than inherit a finished one.
You are mission-driven. You care that European companies build and adopt AI, and you want your work to count toward that rather than toward a job title. You are eager to automate your own work where possible.
AI can do a lot of things, but in the short term, it won't be able to shepherd a growing group of mostly young people in a very dynamic environment. We are looking for someone who can foster the most important human qualities within the organization.
We are looking for a long-term partner, not someone optimizing for their next role.
Personified calmness – You bring order, not chaos. When things get hectic, you're the person who slows down, thinks clearly, and helps others do the same. Your presence makes people feel like things are under control. You instill calmness and continuity in the organization.
Good judgment – You know what matters and what doesn't. You read people well. You understand when to push and when to give space, when something is urgent and when it can wait.
Compassionate and empathetic – You care about the people around you. You understand that behind every missed deadline or dropped ball is a human with hidden context. You hold people accountable with kindness.
Ownership mentality – You see problems and fix them without being asked. You don't wait for permission. You follow through.
Strong communicator – Written and verbal. You can draft important emails or have a difficult conversation with equal skill.
Trustworthy – You'll have access to everything and work directly with the CEO. Discretion and trust are very important.
You are a kind person who cares about the people around you.
The Environment
We work from our office in Berlin, Greifswalder Strasse 212. Everyone works together in person because the hardest problems get solved faster at a whiteboard than in a Slack thread. Conversations happen faster, problems get solved quicker, and we actually know each other.
Days start at 8:30. Lunch & dinner are together. We run, go to the gym, and take care of ourselves. Health is not separate from work here, it is part of how we work well.
The vibe is calm but intense. No one is yelling or panicking. But everyone is working hard on things that matter.

APPLICANTS MUST MEET ALL OF THE FOLLOWING MINIMUM QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS FOR THE POSITION. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume - NOT TO EXCEED 2 PAGES.

Resumes over the 2-page limit, will not be reviewed beyond page 2 or may be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position.

TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume must clearly demonstrate that you possess the following technical qualifications.

TQ 1: Demonstrates executive experience in providing leadership and direction to a complex scientific or technical organization, such as the management or oversight of nationally recognized large-scale research and development facilities or programs.

TQ 2: Demonstrates a general understanding of science and technology, as well as a working knowledge of and ability to oversee a wide variety of business and operational management systems.

EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs.

If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position.

There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people.

ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades.

ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality.

ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable.

Als Sekretär/in der Geschäftsprüfungskommission (GPK) sind Sie Teil des Teams der Finanzkontrolle, welche neben Ihrer Revisionstätigkeit auch das Sekretariat der Geschäftsprüfungskommission des Stadtparlaments führt. In Ihrer Rolle sind Sie für die Organisation der monatlichen GPK\-Sitzungen verantwortlich.

Als Vorbereitung stellen Sie eigenständig einen Traktandenvorschlag zusammen und bereiten sämtliche Unterlagen auf. Während den Sitzungen stellen Sie die anspruchsvolle und umfassende Protokollführung sicher.

Zudem beraten und unterstützen Sie den Präsidenten / die Präsidentin und die Mitglieder der Geschäftsprüfungskommission bei verschiedenen Anliegen. Sie unterstützen die GPK bei der Erarbeitung von Anträgen und stellen den Informationsfluss zwischen der Kommission, dem Stadtrat und der Verwaltung sicher.

Die Geschäftsprüfungskommission und die Finanzkontrolle
Die Geschäftsprüfungskommission prüft die Amtsführung des Stadtrats und der Verwaltung, den städtischen Haushalt und alle Geschäfte, für welche nicht andere Kommissionen zuständig sind. Der Geschäftsprüfungskommission steht zur Erfüllung ihrer Aufgaben die Finanzkontrolle zur Verfügung.

Die Finanzkontrolle der Stadt erfüllt ihren Auftrag als unabhängiges, politisch neutrales Fachorgan der Finanzaufsicht. Die Finanzkontrolle unterstützt den Stadtrat, die Direktionen, die Verwaltung und die Geschäftsprüfungskommission des Stadtparlaments in Fragen der Aufsicht, der Rechnungslegung und der internen Kontrolle.

Are you a resourceful, proactive professional who thrives on anticipating needs and solving problems before they arise?

As an Executive Assistant at Amazon, you will serve as a trusted partner to senior leaders, enabling them to focus on strategic priorities while you manage the complex logistics and operations that keep their organizations running smoothly.

This role offers the opportunity to influence organizational outcomes at country level, collaborate with stakeholders across multiple teams, and drive meaningful improvements to processes that impact how we work. If you are adaptable, detail-oriented, and energized by working in a fast-paced environment, we want to hear from you.

· Manage complex calendars and scheduling for senior leaders, applying an understanding of shifting priorities to ensure the best use of their time across competing demands.
· Plan, organize, and execute events and off-sites, coordinating logistics, managing budgets, and communicating with internal and external stakeholders to deliver seamless experiences.
· Prepare, collect, and curate content on behalf of leaders in partnership with key stakeholders, drafting and editing written communications that reflect appropriate tone and nuance.
· Optimize cross-team procedures and processes, identifying opportunities to simplify workflows and implement best practices that benefit the broader organization.
· Coordinate domestic and international travel arrangements, manage expense reporting, and handle purchase orders while ensuring compliance with applicable guidelines.
A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing your leader's calendar, adjusting meetings based on overnight priority shifts and preparing briefing materials for the day ahead. Throughout the day, you move between coordinating a large team event, resolving a scheduling conflict with external partners, mentoring a newer team member on best practices, and pulling together content for an upcoming leadership review. You balance tactical execution with strategic thinking, always staying one step ahead.

Our team is built on a culture of collaboration, trust, and mutual support. We partner closely with leaders and cross-functional teams to ensure organizational priorities move forward efficiently. We are committed to continuous improvement, always looking for ways to raise the bar on how we operate. If you are excited about working in an environment where your contributions directly impact leadership effectiveness and team success, this is the place for you.

Rockstar is hiring a full-time Front Desk & Customer Service Virtual Assistant on behalf of an animal welfare nonprofit serving a large rural service area.

Many callers are older or don't have reliable internet access, so phone remains their primary way of reaching the organization.
This role is not a message-passing position. The VA needs to actually resolve inquiries on the call itself using established scripts and procedures, not just relay information back to staff. As the organization launches new proactive programs over the coming months, this role also has real potential to expand into supporting those initiatives directly.
About the Client
This organization is an animal shelter serving a large, primarily rural community, taking in thousands of animals each year. They are shifting from a reactive to a proactive model of care, actively developing new outreach and prevention programs so their in-person team can focus more directly on hands-on animal care.

============================================================
Über uns
---------
Die Faitron AG ist ein Schweizer Unternehmen mit Sitz mitten in Zürich. Mit unserer Marke HeatsBox – der weltweit ersten smarten, beheizbaren Lunchbox – begeistern wir über 34'000 Kundinnen und Kunden in mehr als 30 Ländern. Wir sind ein kleines, dynamisches Team mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen und viel Gestaltungsfreiraum.
Deine Rolle
-----------
Als Office Manager bist du die gute Seele unseres Büros: Du sorgst dafür, dass im Alltag alles rund läuft, behältst den Überblick über Administration und Buchhaltung und unterstützt unseren CEO tatkräftig im Tagesgeschäft. Die Stelle ist auf Präsenz vor Ort ausgelegt – du arbeitest grundsätzlich täglich in unserem Büro am Limmatquai in Zürich.
Deine Aufgaben
--------------
* Selbstständige Erledigung administrativer Aufgaben (Korrespondenz, Ablage, Dokumentenmanagement, Datenpflege)
* Organisation und Betreuung des Büros: Bestellungen, Post, Empfang von Gästen, Koordination mit Dienstleistern
* Unterstützung des CEO bei administrativen und organisatorischen Aufgaben sowie bei Besorgungen und Erledigungen
* Mitarbeit in der Buchhaltung: Verbuchung von Debitoren und Kreditoren sowie Mahnwesen
* Ansprechperson für unsere Treuhandgesellschaft und Pflege des Kontakts zum Treuhänder
* Terminkoordination und Vor\-/Nachbereitung von Meetings
* Mithilfe bei internen Anlässen und Teamaktivitäten
* Allgemeine Unterstützung des Teams im Tagesgeschäft
Das bringst du mit
------------------
* Abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung (z. B. KV) oder gleichwertige Qualifikation
* Mindestens 3–5 Jahre Berufserfahrung in Administration, Office Management oder Assistenz
* Idealerweise Grundkenntnisse in Buchhaltung (Debitoren/Kreditoren, Mahnwesen)
* Stilsicheres Deutsch in Wort und Schrift, gute Englischkenntnisse
* Organisationstalent, Zuverlässigkeit und eine exakte, selbstständige Arbeitsweise
* Diskretion und Vertrauenswürdigkeit im Umgang mit sensiblen Informationen
* Hands\-on\-Mentalität: Du packst an, denkst mit und behältst auch in hektischen Momenten den Überblick
* Sicherer Umgang mit MS Office bzw. gängigen digitalen Tools
* Bereitschaft, täglich vor Ort in unserem Büro in Zürich zu arbeiten
